# Channel map

The function operates a small set of public channels, each with a defined job, and
content that fits no channel's job is a sign the content is not ready rather than a
reason to stretch a channel.

The company site carries canonical long-form writing and the published archive. It
is the only channel where the full evidence for a claim lives, and every other
channel ultimately points back to it.

The newsletter carries the cycle's selected findings to readers who asked for them.
Its job is depth for a committed audience; growth mechanics that trade reader trust
for list size are outside its charter.

Professional-network presence carries the company's participation in practitioner
conversations — the replies the discovery workflows qualify — and short adaptations
of published findings. Its job is usefulness in threads we did not start.

Community forums are participation-only: the company answers questions where it has
standing and never runs promotional threads there. The forum presence exists to be
a good citizen of spaces practitioners own.

Press interactions run through the briefing workflow with a designated spokesperson.
No other channel speaks to press, and press questions arriving on other channels are
routed, not answered inline.

A proposed new channel enters this map through the function owner with its job
stated first; a channel without a job produces content without a purpose, and the
map exists to prevent exactly that.

## Dormancy

A channel with no job-fitting content for a quarter goes formally dormant with a
pinned note, rather than limping on filler. Dormancy is honest and reversible;
filler teaches the channel's audience to leave and is neither.
